scenarios.title: An operator names the run, slice, milestone, e2e and e2e-area branches under the default format
scenarios.notes: Run branches.py name in a scratch git repo with no .sdlc/config.json and no --format. Cases: --kind run --n 1 gives sdlc/run-1; --kind slice --id S-001 gives sdlc/S-001; --kind milestone --id M-1 gives sdlc/M-1; --kind e2e --id M-1 gives sdlc/M-1-e2e; --kind e2e-area --id M-1 --area api gives sdlc/M-1-e2e-api. Each exits 0 with one JSON object on stdout, key set exactly ok, command, format, kind, branch, and empty stderr. Check that each branch passes git check-ref-format --branch. Check that the command writes nothing in the repo and creates no ref (treeUnchanged). Also try a .sdlc/config.json with branchFormat absent, empty string and non-string: each must fall back to sdlc/{name}. On the Python API, tail and name give the same tails as the CLI.

scenarios.title: A team format with a prefix or a lowercase placeholder applies to the run, milestone and e2e branches
scenarios.notes: Set the format two ways: .sdlc/config.json branchFormat, and the --format flag (the flag wins). Formats: feature/PROJ-1-{name} gives feature/PROJ-1-M-1, feature/PROJ-1-run-1 and feature/PROJ-1-M-1-e2e. feature/PROJ-1-{name:lower} gives feature/PROJ-1-m-1-e2e and lowercases only the tail, never the prefix. Try a suffix format (x/{name}-wip) and a format with the placeholder first ({name}/sdlc). Property: for generated valid formats, name(fmt, kind, **parts) equals prefix + tail + suffix for each of the three new kinds, and the output field format echoes the format that was used.

scenarios.title: A caller leaves out the part a run, milestone, e2e or e2e-area branch needs
scenarios.notes: CLI: name --kind run with no --n; --kind milestone and --kind e2e with no --id and with --id ''; --kind e2e-area with no --area and with --area ''. Each must exit 2 with exactly one JSON object, ok false, an error that names the missing part (n, id or area), no Traceback on stderr, and no file or ref change. Give the wrong part (--kind run --id 1, --kind milestone --n 1): the error must name the needed part. Python API: tail('run'), tail('milestone', id=''), tail('e2e', id=None) raise Fail, never KeyError or TypeError. tail('run', n=0) gives run-0: 0 is a value, not a missing part.

scenarios.title: A run counter arrives in an edge form
scenarios.notes: --n takes argparse int. Try 0, 1, 12, a huge integer (huge-integers family), -1, 1.5, abc, ' 1', +1, 0x1, 1_000, and unicode digits (unicode-digits family, e.g. Arabic-Indic one). Valid ints must give run-<int as Python prints it>; any accepted value must pass git check-ref-format. Refused values must exit 2 with one JSON error and no Traceback. Do not refute a negative n that gives run--1: ADR-20261009-045048 accepts it as a known gap. Do refute a crash, a Traceback, exit code other than 0 or 2, or a branch git refuses for a non-negative integer. Python API: tail('run', n=True), n='7' and n=7 must give a string tail or raise Fail, never another exception.

scenarios.title: Hostile text arrives in the milestone id or the e2e area
scenarios.notes: Feed --id and --area from the attack-corpus families: traversal, control-chars, flag-like-values, injection, format-strings, unicode-whitespace, unicode-confusables, oversized. The command must never run a shell, never import a planted module (plantDecoy), never write a file or ref, and never print a Traceback. Exit code must be 0 or 2 with one JSON object on stdout. ADR-20261009-045048 says the rows check no id shape, so an accepted malformed id is not a defect in itself. Record as a seed, not a refutation, any accepted value that gives a branch git check-ref-format refuses (for example an id with '..' or a space), because the format check only probes the slice sample S-001. A format-string value such as {name} or %s in --id must appear literally in the branch and must not be expanded.

scenarios.title: The new rows leave the existing slice, state and e2e-area tails and the unknown kinds unchanged
scenarios.notes: Regression of earlier slices at the boundary. tail('slice', id='S-001') is S-001; tail('state', ts='20261008101500') is state-20261008101500; tail('e2e-area', id='M-1', area='api') is M-1-e2e-api; tail('e2e', id='M-1') is M-1-e2e and never collides with an e2e-area tail. --kind verify and --kind attempt still exit 2 with 'no branch name is defined for kind' and no Traceback (S-005 owns them). An unknown --kind such as foo exits 2 and lists the kinds. Property: for every kind in TAILS and generated non-empty parts, tail returns a str and name with sdlc/{name} starts with sdlc/.

tools.purpose: Run branches.py name in scratch git repos with a controlled env; record exit code, JSON stdout, stderr and the tree diff.
Call tail and name through pycall.py with generated formats and parts; check the prefix + tail + suffix property and the Fail-only failure contract.
Supply hostile --id, --area and --n values and a planted decoy module for the CLI.

riskReason: One CLI and Python boundary adds three table rows; a wrong tail gives wrong pushed branch names, but the change is small and easy to see.
notes: Diff for product code: three rows added to TAILS in skills/sdlc/branches.py (run, milestone, e2e); cmd_name is unchanged. No HTTP, async, data, UI or i18n boundary is crossed, so those profiles are not tagged. No spec number applies to these scenarios, so limits is not tagged; the oversized family in VS-5 covers long ids as a robustness check only. Profile order for the cap of 4: cli, contract, security. All three tools exist in .sdlc/testkit.json with a self-test (node --test skills/sdlc/test/testkit/*.test.mjs). Known gap per ADR-20261009-045048: no id shape or sign check; S-007 owns the parse round trip.
